examples.en: I live on the second floor of a multi-unit house.

examples.ko: 다세대 주택은 아파트보다 월세가 싼 편이에요.
examples.en: Rent in a multi-unit house tends to be cheaper than in an apartment.
There are many multi-unit buildings in this alley.

examples.ko: 다세대 주택으로 이사 가려고 알아보고 있어요.
examples.en: I'm looking into moving to a multi-unit house.
Our home is a three-story multi-unit building.
Many multi-unit houses have narrow parking lots.

explain: 한 건물에 여러 가구가 따로 사는 작은 규모의 집을 말하며, 보통 '다세대 주택'으로 써요. 아파트보다 작고 '빌라'라고도 불러요. 부동산에서는 '다가구'와 구분해서 말하기도 해요.
explain_en: It refers to a small building where several households live separately, usually '다세대 주택'. It is smaller than an apartment and is also called '빌라'. In real estate it is sometimes distinguished from '다가구'.

examples.en: They reclaimed part of the sea and built a new airport.
Land for burying garbage is running out.
The city decided not to fill in the tidal flats.

examples.ko: 이 지역은 예전에 호수를 매립한 곳이에요.
examples.en: This area is a place where a lake was filled in long ago.

examples.ko: 쓰레기를 땅에 매립하면 냄새와 오염이 생길 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you bury garbage in the ground, smell and pollution can occur.

examples.ko: 항구 옆 바다를 매립했더니 땅값이 올랐어요.
examples.en: After the sea next to the port was filled in, land prices went up.

explain: 바다나 호수를 메워 땅을 만들 때와 쓰레기를 땅에 묻을 때, 두 가지로 써요. 그냥 '묻다'는 사람이나 물건 모두에 쓰지만 '매립하다'는 넓은 땅이나 쓰레기 같은 큰 규모에 써요. 명사 '매립지'도 함께 알아 두세요.
explain_en: It is used in two ways: filling in sea or lake to make land, and burying garbage in the ground. Plain '묻다' (bury) works for many things, but '매립하다' is for large-scale cases like wide land or waste. Also learn the noun '매립지' (landfill site).

examples.en: This painting is not the original but a reproduction.
The museum is displaying only replicas.

examples.ko: 복제물을 팔 때는 표시를 해야 해요.
examples.en: When selling reproductions, you must label them.
Even though it's a replica, it was made as delicately as the real thing.
It isn't easy to tell a copy from the original.
This replica is smaller than the original.

explain: 그림, 유물, 문서처럼 원본을 똑같이 다시 만든 것이에요. 반대말은 '원본'이나 '진품'이에요. 일상에서는 '복사본'이라고 더 쉽게 말해요.
explain_en: It refers to something made as an exact copy of an original, such as a painting, relic or document. The opposites are '원본' and '진품'. In daily speech people more simply say '복사본'.

en: attachment; being affiliated with a larger body

examples.en: This hospital is affiliated with the university.
The annex building has a library and a cafeteria.
I lost the accessory parts that came with the camera.
Many children attend the elementary school attached to the university.

examples.ko: 이 섬은 큰 섬에 부속된 작은 섬이에요.
examples.en: This island is a small one attached to the larger island.

examples.ko: 부속품은 상자 안에 따로 들어 있어요.
examples.en: The accessories are packed separately inside the box.

explain: '부속'은 큰 기관이나 물건에 딸려 있다는 뜻으로 '대학 부속 병원', '부속 건물'처럼 앞에 붙여 써요. 물건에 딸린 작은 부품은 '부속품'이라고 해요. '소속'은 사람이 어디에 속해 있는지 말할 때 써서 달라요.
explain_en: 부속 means attached to a larger institution or object and goes before the noun, as in 대학 부속 병원 and 부속 건물. The small pieces that come with an item are 부속품. 소속 is different: it describes which group a person belongs to.

examples.en: Please write the company's location on the form.
This building is located in Mapo-gu, Seoul.
Do you know where this school is located?
The head office's location changed, so I fixed the address.

examples.ko: 군청 소재지까지 버스로 한 시간 걸려요.
examples.en: It takes an hour by bus to get to the county seat.

examples.ko: 소재지 확인이 안 되면 신청할 수 없어요.
examples.en: If the location can't be verified, you can't apply.

explain: '소재지'는 건물이나 기관이 자리한 곳이에요. 사람이 사는 곳은 '거주지', 건물 주소는 '주소'라고 해요. 서류나 공문에서 많이 쓰고, '본사 소재지'처럼 기관과 함께 말해요.
explain_en: 소재지 is the place where a building or an organization is located. Where a person lives is '거주지', and a building's address is '주소'. It is common in documents and official notices, together with an organization, as in '본사 소재지'.

dis.h: official place where an organization is situated

p.n: 위치 is the everyday word and can also mean exact position, not only the registered place.

examples.en: Our company is located in Gangnam, Seoul.
That university is located in Busan.
I moved to the city where the head office is located.
The area where the factory is located is quiet.
Do you know where the post office is located?
The hospital is near the station, so it's convenient.

explain: 주소·위치를 공식적으로 말할 때 '~에 소재하다'로 써요. 말로는 '있다'나 '위치하다'가 더 자연스럽고, 서류·뉴스에서는 '소재지'(회사나 기관이 있는 곳)로 자주 봐요. 사람이 있는 곳에는 쓰지 않아요.
explain_en: Used officially for an address or location: '~에 소재하다'. In speech, '있다' or '위치하다' is more natural; in documents and news you often see '소재지' (where a company or office is located). It isn't used for where a person is.

p.n: 자리하다 sounds more descriptive and less official.

examples.en: This company builds apartment complexes.
A professional did the bathroom work.

examples.ko: 다리를 시공하는 데 이 년이 걸렸어요.
examples.en: It took two years to build the bridge.

examples.ko: 바닥 타일을 직접 시공해 보고 싶어요.
examples.en: I'd like to try laying the floor tiles myself.
As soon as the design is done, we'll start construction.
A problem came up during construction and the work stopped.

explain: 시공하다는 설계도대로 건물이나 시설을 실제로 짓거나 설치하는 일이에요. 집수리나 인테리어에서 '시공 업체', '시공비'처럼 많이 들어요. 계획과 도면을 만드는 건 '설계'라고 하니 둘을 구분해서 알아 두세요.
explain_en: 시공하다 means actually building or installing something according to the plans. You hear it in home renovation and interior work, as in '시공 업체' and '시공비'. Making the plans and drawings is called '설계', so keep the two apart.

en: inside of a building; inside of a house

examples.ko: 이 건물은 옥내 주차장이 있어서 비를 안 맞아요.
examples.en: This building has an indoor parking lot, so you don't get rained on.
Please take off your shoes inside the building.
The indoor swimming pool is crowded even in winter.

examples.ko: 비가 오는 날에는 행사를 옥내로 옮기기로 했어요.
examples.en: We decided to move the event indoors on rainy days.

examples.ko: 옥내 소화전 위치를 미리 확인해 두세요.
examples.en: Please check the location of the indoor fire hydrant in advance.

examples.ko: 옥내와 옥외 중에서 어디에서 결혼식을 할까요?
examples.en: Should we hold the wedding indoors or outdoors?

explain: 반대말은 '옥외'예요. 안내문이나 시설 설명에서 많이 보이고, 일상 대화에서는 '실내'를 더 많이 말해요.
explain_en: Its opposite is '옥외' (outdoors). You see it on notices and facility descriptions, while in everyday talk people usually say '실내'.

examples.en: The building extension work has started.
The school is noisy because of the addition.

examples.ko: 증축은 허가를 받아야 할 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can only extend a building after getting a permit.
The house extension cost a lot of money.

examples.ko: 증축이 끝나면 교실이 두 개 늘어요.
examples.en: When the extension is done, there will be two more classrooms.
The hospital closed part of it for the extension.

explain: 있는 건물에 층이나 공간을 더 붙이는 건 '증축', 새로 짓는 건 '신축', 허물고 다시 짓는 건 '재건축'이에요. 공사 안내문과 뉴스에서 자주 보여요.
explain_en: Adding floors or space to an existing building is 증축, building a new one is 신축, and tearing down to rebuild is 재건축. You see these on construction notices and in the news.

examples.en: This library has a lot of old publications.
Every publication carries a copyright notice.

examples.ko: 학교에서 만든 출판물도 학생들에게 나눠 줬어요.
examples.en: They also handed out the publications made by the school to the students.

examples.ko: 출판물을 낼 때는 먼저 원고를 꼼꼼히 확인해야 해요.
examples.en: When you put out a publication, you first have to check the manuscript carefully.

examples.ko: 그 회사의 출판물로는 잡지와 책이 있어요.
examples.en: The company's publications include magazines and books.
Illegal publications cannot be sold.

explain: 책, 잡지, 신문처럼 인쇄해서 낸 것을 한꺼번에 가리키는 말이라서 법이나 저작권, 도서관 이야기에서 자주 보여요. 일상에서는 '책'이나 '잡지'처럼 구체적으로 말해요.
explain_en: It is a collective word for printed and published items like books, magazines and newspapers, and it often appears in talk about laws, copyright and libraries. In daily conversation people name the specific thing, like '책' or '잡지'.
